detail.body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: an opt-in `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4` quantizes the GDN `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` of Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 to MXFP4 after load and runs them on AITER MXFP4 GEMMs, because the Quark MXFP4 checkpoints leave both in BF16 and no BF16 kernel beats hipBLASLt on them, worth **-2.0% to -7.0% median TPOT** (+4.8% output tok/s geomean) for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 with NEXTN MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, over 12 serving shapes.

At TP8, `in_proj_qkvz` is a 4608x8192 GEMM per rank and the largest dense weight in every decode and verify step. A new BF16 GEMM tuning table for the MTP shapes gave 99.8% of the throughput of the existing table, and no BF16 kernel we tried beats hipBLASLt on this shape, so the remaining lever is a smaller weight.

## Modifications

- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4`, a comma-separated subset of `in_proj_qkvz,out_proj`. The default is empty.
- `quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py`: `AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`. `quantize_()` quantizes a loaded BF16 weight with the existing `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`, preshuffles the weight (16x16) and the E8M0 scales, and records whether AITER has a tuned preshuffled config for (N, K). `apply()` quantizes the activation with `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`. Up to 64 rows with a tuned config it runs the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle`; everything else runs the ASM `gemm_a4w4(bpreshuffle=True)`.
- `qwen3_5.py`: the variable is read at import and ignored with a warning off gfx95x or without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture` quantizes each named projection before `finalize_fused_in_proj()`. An MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` is no longer an `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, so the packed BF16 qkvz+ba GEMM is not built and `in_proj_ba` (N=32) runs alone in BF16. Only unquantized BF16 projections are converted.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen35_gdn_online_mxfp4.py`: both TP8 shapes at 1, 4, 16, 31, 32, 64, 65 and 256 rows against a dequantized FP32 reference, which covers both sides of the 32-row scale-layout split and the 64-row kernel cut.
- `environment_variables.mdx`: one row for the new variable.

With the variable unset nothing changes: no layer is touched and the packed BF16 path is built as before.

The PR depends on [Rocm/aiter5998](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998) (merged), which adds the tuned preshuffled config for N=4608, K=8192. The AITER pin in `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` (`e7d2453f`) predates it. On that pin `in_proj_qkvz` takes the ASM path at every size: the output is correct, but we have not measured a gain there. The numbers below use an AITER that includes [Rocm/aiter5998](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998).

## Accuracy Tests

The unit test passes on MI355X: relative error below 1e-2 against the dequantized reference for every shape and row count.

End-to-end, with `in_proj_qkvz` only, NEXTN MTP, on the setup under "Speed Tests and Profiling":

| Eval | BF16 (same image and config) | `in_proj_qkvz` MXFP4 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPQA Diamond (thinking, temperature 1.0) | 0.919, 0.929 | 0.914 |
| RULER niah_single_2 64k / 128k | 0.998 / 1.000, 0.996 / 0.998 | 0.998 / 1.000 |

The two BF16 columns are an earlier pair of runs on the same image and config (two BF16 GEMM tuning tables), not part of this A/B. GPQA here has 198 questions and sampling, so a 0.01 difference is within noise. Paired GSM8K, GPQA and NIAH for the PR setting (`in_proj_qkvz,out_proj`) against BF16 on one node are running; I will add them here.

Not tested yet: the unit test and the end-to-end runs used this change applied to v0.5.21 (the class, the method and the test in this commit are byte-identical), not a build of main. Only Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 was run, and only with NEXTN MTP.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, one node, both arms in one job. ROCm v0.5.21 image with #39069, #40708 and #41899, AITER including [Rocm/aiter5998](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998). NEXTN (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens), ReplaySSM, `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`, page size 16, fp8 KV cache, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`. `bench_serve` random dataset, range ratio 0.8. BF16 is the control: the patch is present and the variable is unset.

| ISL / OSL | Concurrency | TPOT BF16 (ms) | TPOT MXFP4 (ms) | TPOT | Output tok/s | Accept length BF16 / MXFP4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 5.75 | 5.56 | -3.3% | (see below) | 4.00 / 4.00 |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 7.82 | 7.56 | -3.3% | +2.5% | 3.99 / 4.00 |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 11.35 | 11.12 | -2.0% | +2.2% | 3.99 / 3.99 |
| 8k / 1k | 32 | 17.69 | 17.00 | -3.9% | +1.8% | 3.98 / 3.98 |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 28.54 | 27.14 | -4.9% | +4.5% | 3.99 / 3.99 |
| 8k / 1k | 128 | 48.06 | 45.03 | -6.3% | +6.0% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 8k / 1k | 256 | 93.19 | 88.01 | -5.6% | +6.1% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 16.36 | 15.22 | -7.0% | +5.9% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 59.84 | 56.58 | -5.4% | +5.9% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 60k / 600 | 64 | 243.10 | 228.00 | -6.2% | +6.4% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 128k / 1k | 4 | 19.62 | 18.58 | -5.3% | +6.0% | 3.99 / 3.98 |
| 128k / 1k | 16 | 80.88 | 77.10 | -4.7% | +5.3% | 3.99 / 3.99 |

The control's 8k / c4 output tok/s (251) is an outlier: both MXFP4 runs on the same node read 575-591 with only 2-3% lower TPOT. That cell is left out of the +4.8% geomean.

`in_proj_qkvz` alone gives -2.2% to -5.0% TPOT on the same node. Adding `out_proj` is faster in 11 of 12 cells.

Per-call time on one MI355X GPU, MXFP4 including the activation quant (us):

| Rows | Packed BF16 qkvz+ba | MXFP4 qkvz | BF16 ba alone | BF16 out_proj | MXFP4 out_proj |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 16.4 | 6.8 | 3.3 | 6.1 | 4.4 |
| 4 | 16.7 | 7.3 | 5.6 | 7.0 | 4.8 |
| 16 | 22.8 | 8.1 | 8.0 | 5.9 | 5.1 |
| 64 | 21.7 | 11.9 | 8.1 | 7.9 | 7.0 |
| 256 | 38.6 | 22.3 | 8.5 | 16.1 | 8.0 |

A run on the stock v0.5.21 image (only #39069 added, for the NEXTN draft path) with and without the variable is queued; I will add it here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Speed is above; accuracy for `in_proj_qkvz,out_proj` is running.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+class AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod(LinearMethodBase):
+    """MXFP4 GEMM for a loaded BF16 linear, quantized once by ``quantize_``.
+
+    The weight and its E8M0 scales are stored preshuffled. Batches of at most
+    ``PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M`` rows run the Triton preshuffled GEMM when AITER ships
+    a tuned config for (N, K); everything else runs the ASM ``gemm_a4w4``.
+    """
+
+    PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M = 64
+
+    @classmethod
+    def quantize_(cls, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_scale, shuffle_weight
+        from aiter.ops.triton._triton_kernels.gemm.basic.gemm_afp4wfp4 import (
+            _get_config,
+        )
+
+        w = layer.weight.data
+        n, k = w.shape
+        # gemm_a4w4 and the preshuffled scales read whole 256x256 tiles.
+        assert w.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and n % 256 == 0 and k % 256 == 0, (
+            f"online MXFP4 needs a BF16 weight with N, K % 256 == 0, got {w.dtype} {n}x{k}"
+        )
+        w_q, w_s = _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig(w)
+        layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            shuffle_weight(w_q.view(torch.uint8), layout=(16, 16)),
+            requires_grad=False,
+        )
+        layer.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            shuffle_scale(w_s.view(torch.uint8)), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        layer.mxfp4_preshuffle_tuned = _get_config(
+            cls.PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M, n, k // 2, True
+        )[1]
+        layer.quant_method = cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        raise NotImplementedError("use quantize_() on a loaded BF16 linear")
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from aiter import gemm_a4w4, per_1x32_f4_quant_hip
+        from aiter.ops.triton.gemm_afp4wfp4 import gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle
+
+        m, n = x.shape[0], layer.weight.shape[0]
+        w_s = layer.weight_scale
+        if m <= self.PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M and layer.mxfp4_preshuffle_tuned:
+            # Below 32 rows the kernel takes un-shuffled activation scales.
+            x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=m >= 32)
+            x_s = x_s.view(torch.uint8)
+            x_s = x_s.view(x_s.shape[0] // 32, -1) if m >= 32 else x_s[:m]
+            y = torch.empty(m, n, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+            gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle(
+                x_q.view(torch.uint8),
+                layer.weight.view(n // 16, -1),
+                x_s,
+                w_s.view(w_s.shape[0] // 32, -1),
+                x.dtype,
+                y,
+            )
+        else:
+            x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=True)
+            y = gemm_a4w4(
+                x_q,
+                layer.weight.view(x_q.dtype),
+                x_s,
+                w_s.view(x_s.dtype),
+                dtype=x.dtype,
+                bpreshuffle=True,
+            )[:m]
+        return y if bias is None else y + bias

+"""ROCm coverage for the online MXFP4 Qwen3.5/3.8 GDN projections."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd")
+
+# Qwen3.8-2.4T TP8: in_proj_qkvz and out_proj.
+SHAPES = ((4608, 8192), (8192, 2048))
+# Both sides of the preshuffled-scale split at 32 rows and of the 64-row cut.
+ROWS = (1, 4, 16, 31, 32, 64, 65, 256)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip and is_gfx95_supported(),
+    "requires AMD gfx95",
+)
+class TestQwen35GdnOnlineMxfp4(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_dequantized_reference(self):
+        from aiter import per_1x32_f4_quant_hip
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes.quark_w4a4_mxfp4 import (
+            AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod,
+            _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16,
+            _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig,
+        )
+
+        for (n, k), m in itertools.product(SHAPES, ROWS):
+            with self.subTest(n=n, k=k, m=m):
+                torch.manual_seed(m)
+                w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
+                x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                w_q, w_s = _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig(w)
+                x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=False)
+                ref = torch.nn.functional.linear(
+                    _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(
+                        x_q.view(torch.uint8), x_s.view(torch.uint8)[:m]
+                    ).float(),
+                    _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(w_q, w_s.contiguous()).float(),
+                )
+
+                layer = torch.nn.Module()
+                layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+                AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod.quantize_(layer)
+                y = layer.quant_method.apply(layer, x)
+
+                self.assertEqual(y.shape, (m, n))
+                rel = ((y.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
+                self.assertLess(rel, 1e-2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
